summary: Stock Minecraft Java Edition 26.1.2 launched through Prism on Linux with Ravel's agent, screen artifact, and native bootstrap only. Injected input followed the ordinary title-screen and world-selection path. Four campaigns are recorded here. The surface campaign re-observed, at 33 callable targets, every row the earlier 31-target campaign had left inherited: the three Ravel screens, the configuration round trip including a restart-required setting, the command and saved-data path, and opt-in profiling. Three of those four passed on their own fresh evidence; profiling did not, because the two longest lines on the report rendered only their tails and the sentence naming what the numbers cannot tell apart was unreadable in the real client. That defect is recorded in `profilingSurfaceDefect`, it was fixed by change `npozznqz`, and the caveat re-observation campaign launched the real client against the fixed screen jar and read the whole report. Every line renders in full at every GUI scale this window offers. With that, every required surface stands observed natively and this record is `pass`. One narrower gap remains open and is named in `openGaps`: nothing on the game's tick path marks a tick boundary, so the collectors' tick counter can never leave zero. The summary no longer states that zero — change `lppyxtnz` names `tick-count` among the metrics this build cannot measure, and that was re-observed in the real client — but the measurement is still missing.

gameDirectory.method: the stock game process working directory was read from outside the process before Ravel was attached

currentCampaign.prismExitNote: The launcher was terminated between launches rather than being allowed to exit on its own. Prism is single-instance, so a launcher left running makes the next `--launch` hand off and return zero having started nothing, and an exit status of zero from it is not evidence that a game ran.

operatorAttestation.worldOpenRoute: Injected input opened the world through the ordinary title screen, Singleplayer world selection, and Play Selected World path. No quick-play or configuration-injected auto-join route was used.

matrixNotCarriedForward.reason: The earlier campaign's matrix is not this campaign's matrix, and the difference is not cosmetic. Two ADG-7 world persistence seams — `world.open-persistence` on `net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.doWorldLoad` and `world.save-persistence` on `net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.saveAllChunks` — entered the reviewed inventory, moving the callable-target count from 31 to 33 over the same 15 classes. A matrix is a claim about a specific set of targets in a specific build, so a count that moved invalidates the reconciliation rather than extending it.
matrixNotCarriedForward.secondReason: The earlier campaign could not have proven the ADG-7 round trip whatever input it received, because no build it ran contained a mod that owns world data. `ravel-composed-host` carried only the configuration mod until change `uyvzkzzs` added `ravel-test-mod-saved-data` to it. That is why M3-W4 and M3-W7 stayed open through the earlier campaign and why its saved-data row persisted a vanilla scoreboard instead of anything Ravel owned.
matrixNotCarriedForward.whatThisMeansForAReviewer: Read the screen, settings, profiling, and command rows below as the earlier campaign's findings at 31 targets, not as this campaign's. They were not re-observed here. Read the rewrite counts, the world persistence round trip, and the instance scan as this campaign's, measured at 33.
matrixNotCarriedForward.howItWasResolved: The surface campaign re-ran the screen, settings, profiling, and command rows against the same build that proved the world round trip — identical agent, screen, and native digests — and its launches reported `rewrote 15 classes and 33 methods` in the agent's own shutdown report. Those rows no longer carry the 31-target campaign's provenance. What remains inherited from it is nothing: the sections below that used to say `Earlier campaign at 31 callable targets` now carry the surface campaign's own observations.

worldPersistenceRoundTrip.scopeOfThisClaim: The rewrite of both persistence methods was already proven in-gate by `jvm/harness/PersistenceMain.java` over eight world lifecycles. What these launches add, and all they add, is the real game's world storage on both ends of that rewrite: an official `SavedDataStorage` writing Ravel's object into an official world directory, and an official world load reading it back and deciding on it.
worldPersistenceRoundTrip.storedObject: data/ravel/mods.dat inside the world directory, written by the game's own SavedDataStorage through dev.ravel.jvm.screen.RavelWorldData

failClosedOnAnUnreadableWorld.method: The stored aggregate's `dataVersion` was rewritten from 3 to 9 outside the game — a version no build declares — and the same world was loaded again through the same Singleplayer route.
failClosedOnAnUnreadableWorld.diagnostic: the world holds `saved_data` saved data at version 9, newer than this build's 3
failClosedOnAnUnreadableWorld.refusalScreenText: This world was not opened. / <diagnostic> / Deleting Ravel's saved data resets Ravel for this world.
failClosedOnAnUnreadableWorld.whatThisProves: The reload did not merely tolerate the stored bytes, it parsed them and decided admission on them. Without this trial, a reload that ignored the aggregate entirely and a reload that read it would look the same from outside.

absentPathObservedSeparately.whatWasObserved: A pre-existing world in the same instance held no `data/ravel` directory before the world round trip campaign's launches and none was created for it, which is the absent-aggregate case ADG-7 initializes fresh state for.
absentPathObservedSeparately.correction: That world now holds a `data/ravel/mods.dat`, written during the world round trip campaign itself rather than by the surface campaign, which never opened it. The observation was true when it was made and is not re-checkable by looking at the instance today. It is left here as a recorded observation rather than a state a reader can go and confirm, and a reader who wants the absent-aggregate case proven fresh should ask for it against a world that has never been opened with Ravel attached.

worldRemovedAfterwards.whenAndWhy: The world created for this campaign was created, hashed, verified across the reload and the refusal trial, and then removed, returning the instance to the single-world shape it had before. A reader should not go looking for it.
worldRemovedAfterwards.whatSurvivesTheRemoval: The proof does not live in that directory. It is the recorded aggregate digest above, the observed reload, and above all the refused load of a stored `dataVersion` rewritten from 3 to 9 — which is what tells a reload that read the bytes apart from one that ignored them. Evidence that needs a private machine-local directory to persist is evidence nobody else can check; a digest is not.

exitRoutes.first: Save and Quit to Title completed and the world's aggregate was written. The window-manager close request was then sent and the game ignored it, continuing to render with no window; the process was terminated with SIGTERM and its shutdown hook ran. This launch is not offered as a clean-exit result.
exitRoutes.second: Save and Quit to Title, then Quit Game from the title menu. Java exited on its own with no signal. This is the clean-exit result.
exitRoutes.third: The world was refused before it opened, so nothing was loaded to quit from; the process was terminated with SIGTERM and its shutdown hook ran.

profiling.optInMechanism: Profiling is not a control on the screen. It is turned on for a launch with the `-Dravel.profiling=true` system property, and the screen says so when it is off: `Profiling is off, so nothing was collected. / Launch with -Dravel.profiling=true to turn it on.` That off-state was observed on the first launch and the on-state on the second, which carried the property.

saved_data - 501310 ns in 6186 calls (6186 ev, 0 cmd)
profiling.countsAdvanceWhileTheScreenIsOpen: The same two rows were read twice a few seconds apart and moved from 5681 to 6186 calls, which is what tells a live report apart from a rendered constant.
profiling.wallClockLine: Slow above 2500 us. Times are wall-clock, not CPU time.
profiling.caveatsDefect: The surface campaign found the caveat and the unsupported-metrics line clipped; see `profilingSurfaceDefect`. Both were fixed by change `npozznqz` and re-observed whole by the caveat re-observation campaign; see `caveatReObservationCampaign`.
profiling.tickAndCommandCountNote: Re-observed after change `lppyxtnz`. The summary line reads `2 mods entered` and states no tick count at all; `tick-count` is named in `Not measurable in this build:` beside the other five metrics. Both mod rows read `(3804 ev, 0 cmd)`. The per-mod call and time figures are real and moving, so the report is collecting. This launch executed no command, so its `0 cmd` neither confirms nor clears the command counter — it is what a run with no commands should show. The earlier campaign's `0 cmd` after four commands through chat is still an unexplained observation and is not addressed here.
profiling.caveatTextAsRendered: A mod is charged for host work it calls back into. The window is entry to return, so a mod that asks Ravel to resolve a registry key is charged for the lookup as well as for its own code.
profiling.provenance: The rows, the opt-in mechanism, the live counts, and the wall-clock line are the surface campaign's observations against the screen jar recorded in `artifacts`. The caveat and unsupported-metric lines are the caveat re-observation campaign's, against the fixed screen jar recorded in `caveatReObservationCampaign`.

rewrite.measuredIn: The three launches of this campaign each reported `rewrote 15 classes and 33 methods` in the agent's own shutdown report, with 675660, 749397, and 28845 native invocations. The figure above is the second launch, which is the one that both read a stored aggregate and exited through Quit Game.

resolvedDeviations.resolution: The accepted second launch used injected input through the ordinary title-screen and Singleplayer world-selection path. It loaded the world-only classes, exercised command and saved-data behavior, saved, relaunched, and verified persistence.

The source-composed production host populated the runtime and configuration stores during premain. The real Mods, settings, and profiling screens opened from the title menu and consumed production Hook data.

Change lwysptxkplzu replaced the classfile API's loading hierarchy resolver with resource parsing, preventing TitleScreen from being defined reentrantly while another class was transformed. Per-class matched-method and failure reporting then reconciled all 15 classes and 31 callable methods with zero transformation failures.

The accepted second launch opened a world, returned through Save and Quit to Title, selected Quit Game, and let both Java and Prism exit naturally. The earlier title-only SIGTERM launches remain historical evidence but are not the passing trial.

excludedRun.reason: The first launch completed the game-side checklist and emitted the exact shutdown report, but HotSpot remained unresponsive after the game stopped. It was excluded, diagnosed privately, and cleaned up. The accepted relaunch repeated the required persistence and world checks and exited naturally.

profilingSurfaceDefect.whatWasObserved: Two of the seven lines on the profiling report render only their tail. The line naming the metrics no collector can measure appears as `-memory, cpu-time, transferred-bytes, saved-data-footprint`, and the accuracy caveat appears as `y key is charged for the lookup as well as for its own code.`, which is not a sentence. The other five lines, all shorter, render in full.

intendedText.unsupportedMetrics: Not measurable in this build: retained-memory, allocated-memory, cpu-time, transferred-bytes, saved-data-footprint
intendedText.accuracyCaveat: A mod is charged for host work it calls back into. The window is entry to return, so a mod that asks Ravel to resolve a registry key is charged for the lookup as well as for its own code.

profilingSurfaceDefect.rootCause: The screen draws every line as a non-editable `EditBox` of fixed width. `EditBox` scrolls its visible window to follow the cursor, and `setValue` leaves the cursor at the end of the string, so any line wider than the widget shows its last characters and hides its first. The window was enlarged from 854x480 to 1400x800 and the same two lines stayed clipped, because the widget width is fixed rather than derived from the screen width, which is what rules out a display-size explanation.
profilingSurfaceDefect.notFixedHere: The fix is small and belongs to the screen rather than to this record. It is deliberately not made in this campaign, because changing the screen jar changes its digest, and every row above was observed against the digest recorded in `artifacts`. Re-observation, not a patch landed after the fact, is what would let those rows keep their provenance.

whatTheClippingCosts.unsupportedMetrics: Two of the five metric names are lost outright, not just the label. The build declares `retained-memory`, `allocated-memory`, `cpu-time`, `transferred-bytes`, and `saved-data-footprint` unsupported; the client shows `-memory, cpu-time, transferred-bytes, saved-data-footprint`, which is the tail beginning inside the word `allocated-memory`. A player reading the screen cannot learn that retained memory and allocated memory are unmeasured, and the fragment `-memory` does not name either of them.
whatTheClippingCosts.accuracyCaveat: The whole sentence is lost but its last clause. What the screen shows has no subject and reads as though some unnamed key were being charged, which is not what the caveat says.

profilingSurfaceDefect.foundBy: the surface campaign, in the real client, at 33 callable targets

fixedBy.description: fix: split the profiling screen's lines to the width it draws them at
fixedBy.mechanism: The screen now splits every line to the width it draws it at before building the widget, using the game's own font (`splitIgnoringLanguage`) against the widget width less the `EditBox` border inset, so no line is ever wider than the box carrying it and no box has to scroll. Splitting spends rows, so the screen also measures the window's row budget and hands it out in a stated order: the summary and the accuracy statement are claimed first and are never cut.

profilingSurfaceDefect.whyThisBlockedTheGate: M3-W6 asks that per-mod attribution accuracy and unsupported metrics be explicit, and M3-W7 asks that every required surface pass natively. Both halves of that M3-W6 requirement failed on the native screen: two of the five unsupported metric names never reach the player, and the accuracy sentence reaches them as a fragment. The screen's own documentation says an unsupported metric is drawn rather than omitted, precisely so it cannot be confused with one that was left out — the clipping reintroduces exactly that confusion for two of them. The report was drawn, so this was not an unreached surface; it was a reached surface that failed. It now passes.

surfaceCampaignPrivateEvidenceDigests.note: Raw game stdout and screenshots were held outside the repository and deleted when the campaign finished. The redacted logs are the sanitized form of the same streams, with filesystem paths, the player name, account and world identifiers, and any port removed; their digests are recorded so a later reader can tell what was hashed.

openGaps.profilingTickCounter: `Profiler::tick` in `crates/ravel-observability/src/profiling.rs` is exercised only by that module's own unit tests and has no caller anywhere in the production graph, so the counter it increments can never leave zero in a real launch. What is fixed is the report, not the measurement: change `lppyxtnz` names `tick-count` among the metrics the payload cannot measure, and the screen drops its tick clause for any metric the payload calls unmeasurable. Re-observed live against the fixed build — the summary reads `2 mods entered` and `tick-count` appears in the unmeasurable line. The gap that stays open is that nothing on the game's tick path marks a tick boundary at M3; wiring one is what would put the clause back, with nothing on the screen to change.
openGaps.profilingCommandCounter: Both mod rows read `0 cmd`. The surface campaign observed this on a launch that executed four commands through chat; this campaign ran no commands, so it neither confirms nor clears it. Recorded as still undiagnosed.

caveatReObservationCampaign.purpose: Confirm in the real client that the profiling report's two longest lines render in full after `npozznqz`, which is the one thing that stood between this record and a `pass`.
caveatReObservationCampaign.scopeDiscipline: Only the profiling surface was claimed. The world round trip, the refused dataVersion load, `current_dir()`, staging, the `-javaagent` attach, the configuration round trip, the command path, and the instance scan were not re-run and keep the provenance they already carried.
caveatReObservationCampaign.whatDiffersFromTheSurfaceCampaignBuild: Exactly one artifact: the screen jar, which carries the fix. The agent jar and the native library are byte-identical to the ones every other row here was observed against, so this launch measures the same 33-target inventory and the same native boundary, and the only thing that changed is the class that drew the clipped lines.
caveatReObservationCampaign.otherScreensInThatJar: The Mods screen and the title-screen entry point ship in the same jar and were passed through on the way to the profiling screen; both looked as the surface campaign recorded them. That is noted as consistency rather than claimed as a re-observation, because their rows were not the object of this campaign.
caveatReObservationCampaign.howProfilingWasTurnedOn: `-Dravel.profiling=true` in the instance's `JvmArgs`, with `OverrideJavaArgs` set true, because Prism silently ignores `JvmArgs` otherwise. There is no in-game toggle; the screen reports the state and never sets it.
caveatReObservationCampaign.playBeforeReading: The instance's one pre-existing world was opened and played for roughly two minutes so the report would carry real rows. No world was created and none was removed; the instance still holds exactly one.
caveatReObservationCampaign.guiScalesOffered: This window (854x480) offers Auto, 1, and 2, and Auto resolves to 2. Both distinct scales were observed; cycling past 2 wraps to Auto, so no larger scale exists here to test.

atDefaultScale.linesDrawn: Seven: the two summary lines, the heading `What these numbers cannot tell apart:`, and the accuracy statement split over four lines, all readable end to end.
atDefaultScale.whatTheRowBudgetCut: The mod table and the unsupported-metrics line. At scale 2 the window has seven rows, and the screen spends them in its stated order, keeping the summary, the heading, and the statement. That is the documented no-scrolling limit behaving as designed, not clipping: nothing drawn is truncated.

atScaleOne.linesDrawn: Twelve, the whole report, re-observed after change `lppyxtnz` on a launch that stayed on the title screen: `2 mods entered`; `Slow above 2500 us. Times are wall-clock, not CPU time.`; `configuration — 510553 ns in 3804 calls (3804 ev, 0 cmd)`; `saved_data — 109520 ns in 3804 calls (3804 ev, 0 cmd)`; `Not measurable in this build: retained-memory, allocated-memory, cpu-time, transferred-bytes, saved-data-footprint, tick-count` split over three lines; the heading; and the accuracy statement split over four. The summary states no tick count and `tick-count` now stands among the metrics this build cannot measure, which is six metrics over the same three wrapped rows the five took. The per-mod figures are lower than the earlier reading of this line because this launch opened no world; they are this launch's numbers, not the earlier campaign's.
atScaleOne.bothLongLinesWhole: The two lines that were clipped before are the two that now wrap. Every metric name reaches the player, including `retained-memory` and `allocated-memory`, which the clipping used to swallow, and the accuracy statement reads as a sentence from its subject to its full stop.
